blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A ReplicaSet keeps a set number of identical Pods running. It comes from the apps/v1 API.
blocks.why: Deployments create ReplicaSets for you and add safe updates. Learn it here, then write Deployments in real projects.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a ReplicaSet, from the apps/v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.what: The name is how you find the ReplicaSet later, for example with kubectl get replicaset web-copies.
blocks.why: Kubernetes starts the name of every Pod it creates for this ReplicaSet with web-copies.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the ReplicaSet
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: web-copies

blocks.title: How many copies?
blocks.what: Replicas is the number of identical Pods to keep running.
blocks.why: If a Pod is deleted or fails, the ReplicaSet starts a new one to get back to this number.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes uses the default of one replica.
blocks.comment: How many copies of the Pod to keep running
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: web-copies
spec:
  replicas: {{replicas}}

blocks.title: Which Pods belong to it?
blocks.what: The selector picks the Pods this ReplicaSet counts: the ones labelled app: web-copies.
blocks.why: The label is different from the Deployment lesson, so the two never fight over the same Pods.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 ReplicaSets must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Count the Pods that carry this label
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: web-copies
spec:
  replicas: {{replicas}}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-copies

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template is the blueprint for every Pod the ReplicaSet creates. It gives each Pod the label app: web-copies.
blocks.why: The template labels must match the selector, or Kubernetes rejects the ReplicaSet.
blocks.ifRemoved: The ReplicaSet would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: The blueprint for each Pod, with the label the selector looks for
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: web-copies
spec:
  replicas: {{replicas}}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-copies
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-copies

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: Each Pod runs one container from the nginx image.
blocks.why: A Pod template needs at least one container. This block makes the file ready to apply.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the ReplicaSet, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: web-copies
spec:
  replicas: {{replicas}}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-copies
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-copies
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.30.4

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. ReplicaSets are in apps/v1.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A ReplicaSet keeps identical Pods running.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The ReplicaSet's name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.spec: The desired state of the ReplicaSet.
notes.spec.replicas: How many Pods to keep running. The default is 1.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this ReplicaSet counts and replaces.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be counted.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: Match Pods whose app label is web-copies.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod this ReplicaSet creates.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets the label app: web-copies, so the selector finds it.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container's name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: The image to run, with a version tag. A fixed tag runs the same version every time.

tryIt.result: DESIRED, CURRENT, and READY all match your replica count.

tryIt.command: kubectl delete pod <name of one web-copies Pod>
tryIt.result: Run kubectl get pods -l app=web-copies again. A new Pod has replaced it.

check.run: kubectl delete $(kubectl get pods -l app=web-copies -o name | head -n 1)

tryIt.result: Removes the ReplicaSet and its Pods.

questions.question: What does replicas: 3 ask for?
answers: Three restarts if a Pod fails
questions.explain: The ReplicaSet keeps three Pods running and replaces any that stop.

questions.question: Why must the label on line 13 match the selector on line 9?
answers: The ReplicaSet counts only Pods with that label
The label sets the Pod name
questions.explain: The selector finds the Pods to count. Pods made from the template must carry the same label.

questions.question: Why do most people write a Deployment instead?
answers: A Deployment manages ReplicaSets and handles updates for you
questions.explain: A Deployment creates a ReplicaSet for you. It also replaces Pods safely when you change the image.

fix.message: Error from server (BadRequest): error when creating "replicaset.yaml": ReplicaSet in version "v1" cannot be handled as a ReplicaSet: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field ReplicaSetSpec.spec.replicas of type int32
fix.explain: Quotes turn 3 into text. replicas needs a number.
